title: finding(plugin-view): `ObjectViewProps.dataSource` is declared REQUIRED while its own JSDoc one line above promises a context fallback — one of the two has been wrong the whole time
body:
Reported by the `#7417` dev seat and **held back** as *"one line of judgement about intent, not a measurement"*. ⭐ The PM seat disagrees on that classification and files it: the contradiction is **visible in the file**, between two lines one apart. What is *not* measurable is which of the two is wrong — and that is precisely what a `finding` card is for.

## The contradiction

`packages/plugin-view`'s `ObjectViewProps` declares:

```ts
dataSource: DataSource;   // required
```

while its own JSDoc, **one line above**, says:

> If not provided, falls back to `SchemaRendererProvider` context.

⇒ The type says a caller **must** pass it. The prose says a caller **may omit** it and the component will resolve it from context. Both are on the published props surface of a component this repo's own documentation now teaches (PR objectui#7836 rewrote the root README's Basic Usage block onto `plugin-view`'s `ObjectView` precisely because it is the spelling that works).

## Which one is wrong is the open question

| if the **type** is right | if the **JSDoc** is right |
|:--|:--|
| the fallback prose is stale and should go — and anyone who read it and omitted the prop got a compile error, so the cost is loud | the prop should be optional, and the type has been refusing a supported call shape the whole time — the cost is silent: nobody ever tried it |

⚠️ **Measure before choosing**: does the component actually consult `SchemaRendererProvider` context when `dataSource` is absent? The answer decides the card, and it is a reading, not a preference.

## Why it is worth a card rather than a passing fix

⛔ Not adjacent enough to fold into anything open. objectui#7483 is about **app-shell's** `ObjectView` having its entire props surface typed `any` — a different component and a different defect (no declaration at all, versus two declarations that disagree).

⚠️ Note the Clause-② shape before anyone picks it up: if the answer is *"the JSDoc is right"*, the repair **widens a published accept set** (a required prop becomes optional) ⇒ Clause-② `yes`, and it does not belong to an ordinary dispatch lane. If the answer is *"the type is right"*, it is a comment deletion ⇒ Clause-② `no`. **The measurement decides which lane can take it**, which is another reason to measure first and rule second.

Related: objectui#7417 · PR objectui#7836 · objectui#7483 (app-shell's `ObjectView`, typed `any`)
